newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Enterprises offers 150 mln shares in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Enterprises offers 150 mln shares in IPO.

text.p: Beijing municipal government controlled Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd said on Monday it would offer 150 million shares in a global initial public offering (IPO) at HK$12.48 per share.
The company said 10 percent of the issue would be offered in a Hong Kong public offering and 90 percent in an international placement.
The issue price represents a price/earnings multiple of 19.35 times on a fully diluted basis and 18.71 times on a weighted average basis, it said.
Beijing Entreprises said it expected combined profits after taxation and minority interests but before extraordinary items of not less than HK$350 million for the year ending December 31, 1997.
The prospective dividend yield is 1.9 percent and adjusted net tangible asset value per share is HK$7.72.
The IPO will run from May 20-23 and dealing in the shares is due to begin on May 29.
Peregrine Capital Ltd and Morgan Stanley Asia Ltd are the joint global coordinators and joint sponsors of the issue.
The company said it had granted underwriters an option to issue 22.5 million shares to cover over-allotment.
Beijing Enterprises is the primary commercial vehicle for the Beijing municipal government to access international markets for capital, technology and management expertise.
The company is a conglomerate involved in retailing, infrastructure, hotel services and the high-tech industry.

The company said the issue would raise net proceeds of about HK$2.19 billion, of which HK$245 million would be used to expand its consumer products subsidiaries, HK$125 million to expand its tourism services, HK$200 million to expand its retail operations and HK$335 million to expand its Jianguo Hotel.
